To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of a transaction routing strategy is highly dependent on the accuracy of the workload and system parameter values used in the response times estimation; (2) the performance of response time based routing strategies can be improved by introducing some global considerations into the decision making process; and (3) adaptive response time based routing can achieve a robust and efficient load distribution.

(a) response time based routing strategies that try to minimize the response times of incoming transactions are sensitive to the accuracy and completeness of information on workload and system characteristics used in response time estimation, and (b) three alternative strategies are proposed that can strike a balance in terms of load balancing, global and individual optimization, and robustness to parameter accuracy and completeness

the response time of a transaction is a function of the workload, the system parameters, and the routing strategy, and that the response time based routing strategies are robust with respect to inaccuracies in the workload and system parameter values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of robust load balancing strategies that are able to cope with the uncertainty inherent in distributed transaction processing systems.
the problem of balancing the load in a distributed database system.
the problem of robustly sharing the workload of a distributed database system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the threshold strategy is the best choice for robust routing, the discriminatory strategy is the best for load balancing, and the adaptive strategy is best for optimizing individual transaction response time.
a strategy that tries to minimize the estimated response time of individual transactions and that is robust with respect to parameter accuracy, is the best strategy to use.
the adaptive strategy is best in terms of response time and throughput, while the discriminatory and adaptive strategies are best in terms of fairness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
response time based transaction routing is an effective strategy that balances the conflicting requirements of load sharing and transaction affinity.
the adaptive strategy performs best and is the most robust, followed by the discriminatory and the threshold strategies.
response time based routing strategies are robust and can be used to effectively share the load among the processing systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a robust routing strategy can be achieved by combining the benefits of both the response time based and the affinity based routing strategies.
a response time based load sharing strategy can be robust with respect as long as the strategy is designed to be robust.
a response time based routing scheme can be robust to parameter inaccuracy if it is designed to take this into account.
